title: Drawing from memory
standfirst: The weekly chart entry is twenty percent of your grade and the most useful thing you will do in this course. It is also the thing people most often do wrong, in a way that costs them nothing now and a lot in December.

sections.h: You are not being graded on the drawing
p: This is not an art assignment and it is not graded on accuracy. It is graded on completion, which means a wrong drawing that you caught and corrected earns full marks.
The reason is simple. The drawing is not the product. The drawing is the instrument that finds out what you actually have in memory, and a drawing made with the book open finds out nothing.
sections.callout: A perfect diagram copied from the book is worth zero to you. I will also be able to tell.

sections.h: The three steps, and why the third one matters most
steps: **Book closed.** Draw the week's mechanism from memory, applied to your patient. Boxes, arrows, labels. Wrong is fine.
**Still closed.** Write three to five lines: what did I leave out, what am I unsure about.
**Now open the book.** Correct your drawing *in a different color* and write one line about what you got wrong.
p: Step three is the whole mechanism. Correcting in a different color leaves the gap visible on the page, which means you can see it, I can see it, and you can find it again in December when you are building the case conference.

sections.h: What a good entry looks like
list: Arrows have directions and the directions are committed to, even when they turn out wrong.
Structures are named, not just drawn.
The correction color is obvious at a glance.
The note underneath says something specific, for example: I had the sensor and the effector but I could not remember what carried the signal.
sections.callout: I need to study more is not a note. I did not know whether the receptor was on the cell surface or inside, that is a note.

sections.h: If drawing by hand is not possible for you
p: Use the drawing canvas on the course site. It takes typed text as well as drawing, so you can build and label the same diagram digitally and it counts exactly the same.
This is a standing option open to anyone for any reason, and you do not need to tell me why you are using it.
Fifteen entries, one per week, all about the same patient. In Week 15 they become your case: you name the condition your patient has and defend it from your own drawings.
That is why the entries are worth doing properly in September. The final is not a separate thing you study for. It is the thing you have been building since Week 1.
